correctness.rationale: For every n>=1 and 1<=r<=n, direct rank-class coordinates yield K((A,B),(C,D))=R(A,D)R(C,B). Choosing each row cut set as a column of its cuts plus n yields a unit lower-triangular p-by-p minor and rank R=p. In an SVD basis K acts as Y->Sigma Y^T Sigma: p positive diagonal modes, one positive and negative for each unordered pair, and p(q-p) zeros. Rank 2 Gram is min(i,j)(n-max(i,j))=n times the inverse Dirichlet Laplacian. Rank n-1 Gram is tridiagonal with diagonals 2, offdiagonals 1. Both trigonometric spectra and determinants follow. The independent finite checker directly compares semigroup inverse equations, transversal Gram, exact rank certificates and all eigenvalues through n=6 in 21 classes; all pass. Finite tests corroborate rather than prove all n.

value.rationale: The full inverse graph is the canonical relation underlying a currently studied semigroup permutation-matching existence problem, but matching existence does not determine the relation spectrum. The classification of exact inertia for every rank and every chain size is structurally complete, with a uniform p^2 rank invariant and nontrivial positive/negative split despite highly variable degrees. Explicit trigonometric spectral lists and determinants in ranks 2 and n-1 give precise analytic refinements. Unlike an arbitrary slice or textbook exercise, this is a natural algebraic invariant of a defined infinite class.
